newsitem.title: UK: Bridon to enhance FKI earnings in first year.
newsitem.headline: Bridon to enhance FKI earnings in first year.

text.p: British engineering company FKI Plc said on Monday its 131 million stg agreed bid for wire rope and lifting systems maker Bridon Plc would enhance its earnings within first year of its ownership.
FKI's chief executive Bob Beeston said the company was expecting to reap "substantial" pricing benefits and discounts out of its planned buyout of Bridon.

FKI earlier announced that it would pay 175 pence for each Bridon ordinary share, representing a premium of 65 percent to its mid-market price on June 27, the last trading day before Bridon announced it was in talks with FKI on June 30.
The combination of Bridon and FKI's material handling division is expected to position the enlarged FKI group as one of the world's leading suppliers of lifting hardware.
"We believe the returns from Bridon will be similar to what we achieved from FKI in the past three years," Beeston said after announcing details of the transaction.
He said FKI was confident of maintaining at least seven percent return on sales for Bridon.
He cited Bridon's markets in the Norwegian region, the Middle East and the Far East as main strengths that could add value to FKI.
FKI also said it had purchased 22.32 million shares, representing 29.9 percent in Bridon at the offer price.
Bridon's share price was up 35 pence at 172 1/2. FKI's share price, however, slipped three pence to 157 1/2.
Beeston said FKI was absorbing 40 million stg of Bridon's debt, taking the larger company's gearing to 114 percent.
Bridon had reported a consolidated profit on ordinary activities before taxation of 7.3 million stg in the year to December, 1996 on a turnover of 361.8 million.
Beeston said it would announce further details on its strategy on Bridon in three months. He said the company was yet to decide whether it would retain the entire 3,000-strong workforce of Bridon.
